result.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
result.summary: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation. We introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs. 63.3 gFD) with 18.2$\times$ less pretraining compute. Further, Halcyon-1.6B outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (35.3 vs. 41.0 gFD) with 275$\times$ less pretraining compute. Controlled experiments show that text-only pretraining does not improve T2I generation. Halcyon also learns image captioning by replacing caption dropout with I2T supervision, maintaining competitive T2I generation quality under the same pretraining budget. We show that strong T2I systems can be trained from scratch without internet-scale language pretraining. Code and models are available at https://cs.stanford.edu/~keshik/halcyon

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Halcyon 系列早期融合（early-fusion）多模态自回归模型，完全从零在 1 亿图文对上预训练来做文生图，并用对照实验考察语言预训练是否必要。
AI.relevance_reason: 其早期融合共享自回归状态、以及「纯文本预训练不提升生成」这一训练对照结论，可供核查语言预训练与融合方式对 VLM 内部视觉状态保留的影响，但论文本身不做推理，联系需人工确认。
